\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic is the data\sphinxhyphen{}analysis layer in the Pluss stack. It gives you three related models:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindle}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bundle}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Slot}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is organized the same way users usually approach the library:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} for table\sphinxhyphen{}style analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} when you want typed column operations outside a frame

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}} when streams/case\sphinxhyphen{}aligned data are a better fit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}} when you want heterogeneous record bundles

\end{itemize}

\chapter{PlussMic User Manual}
\label{\detokenize{manual:plussmic-user-manual}}\label{\detokenize{manual::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is the long\sphinxhyphen{}form guide for PlussMic, the data\sphinxhyphen{}analysis layer of the
Pluss ecosystem. It is written for readers who want to use PlussMic as a daily
tool, not only look up signatures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic has three related models:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
table  \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} DataFrame, Thread, Atlas
kindle \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Stream, Catalog, Archive
bundle \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Slot, Registry, Aisle
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most users start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, because it is the table abstraction used for
CSV, Excel, JSON, Parquet, feature engineering, exploratory analysis, plotting,
and export. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is the typed column model underneath \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}
stacks related frames. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Kindle}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Bundle}} are lower\sphinxhyphen{}level record/stream
models used when the data is not naturally just a rectangular table.


\section{How to read this manual}
\label{\detokenize{manual:how-to-read-this-manual}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read Part I and Part II in order. After that, jump to the chapters that match
your task:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading files: Part III.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loading and saving files: Part IV.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cleaning and transforming tables: Part V.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Column\sphinxhyphen{}level operations: Part VI.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query expressions and SQL: Part VII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time series: Part VIII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Plotting: Part IX.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multi\sphinxhyphen{}frame Atlas data: Part X.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Kindle and Bundle models: Part XI and Part XII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recipes: Part XIII.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Production debugging: Part XIV.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The API reference pages remain the authority for exact overload lists. This
manual explains how to choose and combine those APIs.


\section{Example policy}
\label{\detokenize{manual:example-policy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual does not use one token example per feature. Important APIs are
shown in several contexts: a minimal call, a realistic workflow, option and
error cases, and combinations with adjacent APIs. A short example teaches the
shape of a call; later examples teach how to use it in a program.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In\sphinxhyphen{}memory frames are created directly when the lesson is about table
operations. I/O chapters use files such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"sales.csv"}} and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"transactions.parquet"}}, assumed to be in the program’s working directory.
The manual shows the relevant input file contents before the code. Public
examples never contain paths from the author’s machine.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Pluss values are passed directly where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} conversion is implicit:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sales}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Accra}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{Tema}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{7.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} construction appears only when the example needs Thread
metadata, a validity mask, or a named standalone column.

\subsection{Part I: Orientation}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:part-i-orientation}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic exists to make C++ data work practical. It gives you table loading,
typed columns, missing\sphinxhyphen{}data handling, display, summarization, plotting,
time\sphinxhyphen{}series operations, and conversions into more general record models.


\subsubsection{What PlussMic is for}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:what-plussmic-is-for}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use PlussMic when you want to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
load CSV, TXT, Excel, JSON, or Parquet data into C++;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
inspect and summarize a dataset;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
select, rename, reorder, derive, and transform features;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filter cases with masks or query expressions;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
handle missing numeric, text, and time values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
group, aggregate, pivot, and correlate data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
build plotting outputs from table data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
represent a stack of related tables with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
convert rectangular data into stream/catalog or registry/slot models;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
save cleaned data back to common file formats.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{The three PlussMic layers}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:the-three-plussmic-layers}}

\subsubsection{The core table model}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:the-core-table-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic uses this table hierarchy:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Atlas \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} DataFrame \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Thread \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Series / Note / Timeline / TimeIndex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} owns feature names and feature columns. Each feature is a
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} wraps one core PlussQit payload kind:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} for numeric and boolean data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} for text data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} for datetime\sphinxhyphen{}like data;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} for time\sphinxhyphen{}index data.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This design is why a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} can contain numeric, text, and time features
without losing type\sphinxhyphen{}specific operations.


\subsubsection{Cases and features}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:cases-and-features}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic documentation uses two axis names:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{case} is a row\sphinxhyphen{}like observation.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{feature} is a column\sphinxhyphen{}like variable.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common shape calls:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rows}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ncases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cols}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{nfeatures}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{feature\PYGZus{}names}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this language when reading APIs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(...)}} selects or returns columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cloc(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(...)}} operate in row space.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_cases(...)}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset\_cases(...)}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{align\_cases(...)}} manage the case axis.

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Functional style}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:functional-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Most table operations return a new object:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillna}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sorted}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{cleaned}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{balance}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Mutating operations use a trailing underscore:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillna\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{rename\PYGZus{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{old\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{new\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer the non\sphinxhyphen{}mutating form while learning. Use mutating methods only when you
intentionally want to update an owned object.


\subsubsection{What a beginner should learn first}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part01_orientation:what-a-beginner-should-learn-first}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load a CSV with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame::load\_csv}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inspect with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{info}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select features with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filter cases with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Derive features with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_features}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Summarize with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aggregate}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tally}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_csv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_excel}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_json}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{save\_parquet}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Everything else in PlussMic builds on those ideas.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Part II: Installation, Includes, and Build Setup}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:part-ii-installation-includes-and-build-setup}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic is usually consumed through the Pluss SDK. In a downstream project,
link \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Pluss::SDK}} and include either the Pluss umbrella header or the PlussMic
module header.


\subsubsection{Recommended include}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:recommended-include}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For applications:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For code that only wants PlussMic:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/mic.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}pluss/mic.h\textgreater{}}} includes table, loader, Kindle, and Bundle surfaces:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/bundle/bundle.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/kindle/kindle.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/loader/loader.h\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZdq{}pluss/table/table.h\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
It also includes PlussPl when available, which enables table plotting.


\subsubsection{Minimal consumer CMake}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:minimal-consumer-cmake}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{cmake\PYGZus{}minimum\PYGZus{}required}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{VERSION}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{3.28}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{project}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{plussmic\PYGZus{}app}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{LANGUAGES}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{CXX}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}STANDARD}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}STANDARD\PYGZus{}REQUIRED}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{ON}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{CMAKE\PYGZus{}CXX\PYGZus{}EXTENSIONS}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{OFF}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{find\PYGZus{}package}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{Pluss}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{CONFIG}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{REQUIRED}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{add\PYGZus{}executable}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{plussmic\PYGZus{}app}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{main.cpp}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{target\PYGZus{}link\PYGZus{}libraries}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{plussmic\PYGZus{}app}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{PRIVATE}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{Pluss::SDK}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Configure against a staged SDK:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}S\PYG{+w}{ }.\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}B\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}DCMAKE\PYGZus{}PREFIX\PYGZus{}PATH\PYG{o}{=}/path/to/pluss\PYGZhy{}sdk
cmake\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build\PYG{+w}{ }build
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{revenue}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{120.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{95.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{140.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\subsubsection{Development build inside this repository}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:development-build-inside-this-repository}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
From the repository root:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

PlussMic/examples/table/
PlussMic/examples/kindle/
PlussMic/examples/bundle/

\subsubsection{Header choices}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part02_installation:header-choices}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use broad headers while learning:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use module headers for production libraries with tighter dependencies:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/mic.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/table/table.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/loader/loader.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/kindle/kindle.h\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/bundle/bundle.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use source\sphinxhyphen{}local headers only when working inside the Pluss repository.

\subsection{Part III: The Table Model}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:part-iii-the-table-model}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This part explains how \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}
relate. Understanding these types makes the rest of PlussMic predictable.


\subsubsection{Thread}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:thread}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is one typed column. It can hold one of four payload kinds:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{numeric}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{red}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{green}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{blue}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{dates}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}timeline}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}02T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}03T00:00:00Z}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Inspect a thread:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{defined}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{info}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Access the payload only after you know the kind:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadKind}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{as\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\subsubsection{Missingness and validity}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:missingness-and-validity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} can carry a validity mask. Loader\sphinxhyphen{}created columns use this to represent
missing values from input files.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{missing}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{present}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{notnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{filled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{fillna}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{complete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropna}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric threads also support \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnan}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isfinite}}.


\subsubsection{DataFrame}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part03_table_model:dataframe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} is a set of named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} features with an optional case axis.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{reset}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{indexed}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{reset\PYGZus{}cases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{CSV}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:csv}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Minimal CSV load:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{data.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the correct first call when the file is a conventional comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated
file with a header row. PlussMic reads the header, infers feature types, creates
default numeric case labels, and returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The loader has two public configuration styles:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
initializer\sphinxhyphen{}list config entries, which are compact and convenient;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
typed option structs, which are explicit and better for production code.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Limit cases and select features with config entries:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bank\PYGZhy{}full.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{ncases}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{features}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{age}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{job}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{balance}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{duration}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} for explicit control:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ReadCsvOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{;}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ncases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{age}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{job}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{balance}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{duration}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{job}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Warn}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{bank\PYGZhy{}full.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ReadCsvOptions}} when the ingestion behavior matters. It is easier to
read in code review, safer to extend, and maps directly to the source\sphinxhyphen{}level CSV
loader API.


\subsubsection{CSV mental model}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:csv-mental-model}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV loading has five stages:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read records from the source.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide the header and feature names.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide which input columns become features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Decide whether one input column becomes the case axis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert selected columns into typed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most surprising loading behavior comes from mixing up stages 3 and 4. If a
column is selected as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}}, it becomes the DataFrame case axis and is not
also emitted as a normal feature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ReadCsvOptions}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} column is still used, but it is used as the case axis. The output
features are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{units}}.


\subsubsection{Header handling}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:header-handling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For ordinary files:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header\PYGZus{}row}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For files without a header:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{names}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}} is false and you do not provide names, PlussMic generates feature
names from column positions. For durable code, provide \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{names}} explicitly.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header\_row}} when the actual header is not the first physical row:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{header\PYGZus{}row}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Rows before the header row are skipped from data interpretation.


\subsubsection{Feature projection}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:feature-projection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use names when the file has stable headers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use indices when working with headerless files or unstable external labels:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If both \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{usefeats\_idx}} are empty, all non\sphinxhyphen{}case columns are
loaded. If a requested name is missing, loading fails. If a requested index is
out of range, loading fails.


\subsubsection{Case columns}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:case-columns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The case axis is PlussMic’s row\sphinxhyphen{}label axis. It is similar to an index in other
dataframe libraries, but the public method names use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cases}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a named case column:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use a positional case column:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col\PYGZus{}idx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
After loading, inspect the case axis:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{cases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Move a case axis back into the feature axis later with:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}id\PYGZus{}feature}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{reset\PYGZus{}cases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Verified example: semicolon CSV with case column}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:verified-example-semicolon-csv-with-case-column}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assume the program and this \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sales.csv}} file are in the same directory:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
id;city;region;units;price
A001;Accra;south;10;3.0
A002;Tema;south;7;4.0
A003;Kumasi;middle;12;2.5
A004;Tamale;north;5;5.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sep}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{;}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{case\PYGZus{}col}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{usefeats}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ncases}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{DataFrame}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{sales.csv}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{case dtype=}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{cases}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This example uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_csv\_records}} instead of a file. It is useful for tests,

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{Type inference and explicit dtypes}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:type-inference-and-explicit-dtypes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV data starts as text. PlussMic converts each selected column into a typed
Thread. Common inferred outputs are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
integer Series for integral values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
floating Series for decimal values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
boolean Series for configured true/false tokens;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note for general text;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Timeline or TimeIndex when date parsing is requested.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default boolean token sets include values such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{yes}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype}} when a column must have a specific interpretation:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{customer\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{string}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{int64}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{price}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{float64}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{parse\_dates}} when text columns should become time payloads:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}dates}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{created\PYGZus{}at}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{updated\PYGZus{}at}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{infer\PYGZus{}datetime\PYGZus{}format}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dayfirst}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use explicit dtypes for identifiers that look numeric. Postal codes, account
numbers, and product IDs should usually be loaded as text, not numbers.


\subsubsection{Missing values}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:missing-values}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
CSV missing\sphinxhyphen{}value handling is controlled by:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{na\PYGZus{}filter}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{keep\PYGZus{}default\PYGZus{}na}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{na\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{insert}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{missing}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{na\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{insert}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{N/A}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{na\_filter = false}} disables missing\sphinxhyphen{}value detection. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{keep\_default\_na = true}}
keeps the built\sphinxhyphen{}in missing tokens. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{na\_values}} adds project\sphinxhyphen{}specific tokens.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Missingness becomes a Thread validity mask. That means a numeric feature can
still have an integer or floating dtype even when some rows display as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}.


\subsubsection{Bad lines}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:bad-lines}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Malformed rows are rows whose field count does not match the expected layout.
The policy is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Error}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Warn}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{on\PYGZus{}bad\PYGZus{}lines}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{BadLinePolicy}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Skip}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Error}} for production ingestion when malformed data should stop the job.
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Warn}} when you want diagnostics and can tolerate dropped rows. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skip}}
only when silent row loss is acceptable in that context.


\subsubsection{Engine selection}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:engine-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The CSV engine can be selected explicitly:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{engine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CsvEngine}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Auto}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{engine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CsvEngine}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Parallel}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{options}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{engine}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{loader}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{CsvEngine}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Serial}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Auto}} is the right default for most users. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Parallel}} for large local
files when throughput matters. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Serial}} when debugging parser behavior or
when deterministic step\sphinxhyphen{}by\sphinxhyphen{}step ingestion is more important than speed.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\subsubsection{I/O checklist}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part04_io:i-o-checklist}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use typed options for production ingestion.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set separators explicitly for non\sphinxhyphen{}comma files.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{case\_col}} deliberately when a dataset has an ID column.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Limit with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ncases}} while developing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{on\_bad\_lines = Warn}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Skip}} only when dropping malformed rows is acceptable.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Save cleaned outputs with explicit format\sphinxhyphen{}specific filenames.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename}} changes one feature name and fails if the old name is missing or the
new name already exists. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename\_features}} applies several renames one after
another. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{relabel\_features}} replaces the entire feature axis, so the number of
new names must match the current feature count. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder}} also requires the
full feature set; it is not a selector. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features(\{...\})}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(\{...\})}}
when you want to keep only part of the frame.

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{first}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{cloc}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sampled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sample}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view}} are preview\sphinxhyphen{}oriented and return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrameView}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample}} return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(start, stop)}} uses half\sphinxhyphen{}open row positions: it keeps \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} and stops
before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}}. Negative slice bounds are normalized against the frame size by
the implementation. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(indices)}} uses the exact row positions you provide
and keeps them in that order. Both preserve the selected rows’ original case
labels.

The first table is sorted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{price}} descending. The case labels still show
the original row labels, so the first row displays case \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}} because Tamale was

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second table is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(1, 3)}}. It keeps row positions 1 and 2 and stops
before position 3. The third table is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(\{3, 0\})}}; it keeps exactly Tamale
then Accra because that is the order of the indices.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fourth table demonstrates feature\sphinxhyphen{}axis work. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename("units", "quantity")}}
changes the feature name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop(\{"region"\})}} removes the region feature, and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder(\{"city", "price", "quantity"\})}} arranges the full remaining feature
set in the requested order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The fifth table shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{set\_cases("city", true)}}. City values become case labels,
and the original \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city}} feature is removed because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{drop\_feature}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}.
The sixth table shows \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reset\_cases("city\_case")}}, which turns the case axis
back into a normal feature named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{city\_case}} and restores default numeric case
labels.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} when two frames already have compatible row counts and you want to
append features. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stitch\_on}} when rows must be matched by key values. Use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}} when the right frame should patch values into the left frame. Use
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine}} when you need the configurable primitive behind \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The names are precise:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} is feature\sphinxhyphen{}wise combination. It requires the same case count and
appends right\sphinxhyphen{}hand features by row position. Duplicate feature names receive
the collision suffix.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}} is schema\sphinxhyphen{}preserving patching. It only updates overlapping features
and ignores right\sphinxhyphen{}hand features that do not exist on the left.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stitch\_on}} is key\sphinxhyphen{}based matching. It creates rows for matching key values
and appends right\sphinxhyphen{}hand payload features.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{combine}} is the configurable primitive underneath \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}}.

\end{itemize}

\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
0    | B     2     20         5
1    | C     3     30         8
\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}
[2 cs x 4 feat]
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}}. The left frame has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sku}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}}; the patch frame
has \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}}. Because \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} exists on both sides, PlussMic keeps the
left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} and appends the right feature as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty\_patch}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}} is appended
without renaming.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The second result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{update}}. Only overlapping features are considered, so
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} is replaced by the patch values and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status}} is ignored. This is useful
when the right frame is a correction frame rather than a source of new columns.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stitch\_on("sku", right, "sku", "\_right")}}. This is the
key\sphinxhyphen{}based operation. Only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} appear because those keys exist in both
frames. The right key feature is not duplicated because both key names are
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sku}}. The right \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}} collides with the left \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty}}, so it becomes
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{qty\_right}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cost}} is appended as a new payload feature.

\subsection{Part VI: Thread Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:part-vi-thread-workflows}}\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is PlussMic’s column model. Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} feature is a named
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, and many table operations delegate their real work to Thread methods.
If \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} is the table abstraction, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} is the typed one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional
array abstraction underneath it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A Thread has four important pieces of state:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a payload family: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
an optional validity mask for missing values;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
optional display labels;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
an optional display name.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The payload family controls which operations are legal. Numeric arithmetic is
for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} threads. Text cleaning is for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Note}} threads. Calendar extraction
is for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Timeline}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TimeIndex}} threads. Missingness is tracked separately
through the validity mask, so a row can have a stored payload value and still
display as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}.


\subsubsection{Payload families}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:payload-families}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The public kind enum is:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{enum}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{class}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nc}{ThreadKind}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Note}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{Timeline}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n}{TimeIndex}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the family\sphinxhyphen{}specific accessors only after you know the kind:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadKind}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{as\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadKind}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Note}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{as\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling the wrong accessor is an error. For example, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{as\_series()}} is only valid
for a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} payload.


\subsubsection{Construct threads}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:construct-threads}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric values normally enter a Thread through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::make\_series}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Text values normally enter through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::make\_note}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{text}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}note}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{alpha}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{beta}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{gamma}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You can attach a validity mask at construction time:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{make\PYGZus{}series}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{4.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{valid}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Series}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{zeros}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{codem}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Bool}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{valid\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{reinterpret\PYGZus{}cast}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{bool}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{valid}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{raw\PYGZus{}data}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{valid\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{valid\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{valid\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{valid\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{valid\PYGZus{}ptr}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{score}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{valid}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The third row stores \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.0}} in the payload, but its mask value is false. Display
and null\sphinxhyphen{}aware operations treat that row as missing.


\subsubsection{Inspect a Thread}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:inspect-a-thread}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use these methods when writing generic code:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{defined}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{unique}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{size}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{kind}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dtype\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{has\PYGZus{}validity\PYGZus{}mask}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}valid}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dtype\_name()}} reports the payload dtype, such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float64}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{utf8}}. It does
not tell you whether the thread has missing values. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{has\_validity\_mask()}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notnull()}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{is\_valid(row)}} for that.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Display and debug methods:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{info}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_string()}} is useful in tests, examples, and documentation because it uses
the same display path a user sees.

\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{units clipped:}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{units}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{clip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{6.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{10.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{cout}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{city lower:}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{city}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{lower}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}string}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+sc}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{;}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

1  7

3  6

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features("units")}} returns a numeric Series\sphinxhyphen{}backed Thread. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clip(6.0, 10.0)}}
clamps values below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}} upward and values above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}} downward. The original
unit values are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{12}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}}, so the result is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{10}},
and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{features("city")}} returns a Note\sphinxhyphen{}backed Thread. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lower()}} returns lower\sphinxhyphen{}case
city names. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contains("a")}} returns a boolean \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}}, which the example wraps
as a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} only so it prints in the same format.


\subsubsection{Row\sphinxhyphen{}space operations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:row-space-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A Thread is one\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional, so row\sphinxhyphen{}space operations work directly on element
positions:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{tail}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{view}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{slice}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{take}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{vector}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{k+kt}{int64\PYGZus{}t}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{8}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{shift}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sort\PYGZus{}values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropna}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{distinct}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{head}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tail}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{view}} return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ThreadView}}, which can auto\sphinxhyphen{}render. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dropna}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distinct}} return ordinary
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} values.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{slice(start, stop)}} is half\sphinxhyphen{}open. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(indices)}} keeps exactly the requested
positions in exactly that order. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{shift(periods)}} moves values by row offset
and marks the newly exposed edge as missing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values(ascending, nulls\_last)}} sorts the valid values and places masked rows according to
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last}}.


\subsubsection{Missingness}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:missingness}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Missingness is mask\sphinxhyphen{}based. A Thread without a validity mask has no mask\sphinxhyphen{}level
missing values. A Thread with a validity mask uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for present and
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} for missing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Common methods:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{missing}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{present}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{notnull}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{complete}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{dropna}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{forward}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{ffill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{backward}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{bfill}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Numeric checks are separate:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{nan}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isnan}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{finite}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{isfinite}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnan()}} checks floating\sphinxhyphen{}point NaN in a Series payload. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} checks the
Thread validity mask. A value can be finite but masked out, and it will still
display as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}.

The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}} payload has five numeric values, but row 2 is masked as missing,
so it displays as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{isnull()}} is the logical inverse of the validity mask.

values for them, and also carries the original missing row forward so row 4 is
missing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort\_values}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nulls\_last=false}} places the missing value first,
then sorts valid values ascending. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take(\{4, 1, 0\})}} keeps rows 4, 1, and 0, in

\subsubsection{Numeric operations}
\label{\detokenize{manual/part06_thread_workflows:numeric-operations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Series\sphinxhyphen{}backed Threads support arithmetic, comparisons, math transforms, rolling
windows, and scalar reductions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Arithmetic can be written through methods or operators:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{plus\PYGZus{}two}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{+}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{doubled}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{ratio}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numerator}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{denominator}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{remainder}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Comparison operators return boolean Series\sphinxhyphen{}backed Threads:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{positive}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{in\PYGZus{}limit}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{same}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{left}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{right}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Named numeric transforms:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{absolute}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{abs}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{clipped}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{clip}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.0}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{logged}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{log}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{exponentiated}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exp}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reductions return scalar \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} values, not raw C++ scalars:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{item}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{total}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{item}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{sd}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{std}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{item}\PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}}\PYG{k+kt}{double}\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Available reductions include:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{count}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{any}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{all}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{median}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{min}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{corr}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{other}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corr}} accepts a method:

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rolling\PYGZus{}min}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{window}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadWindowOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RollingMin}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{rolling\PYGZus{}max}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kr}{thread}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{window}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{table}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ThreadWindowOp}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{RollingMax}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The arguments are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{window}}: number of rows in the trailing window;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}: rolling operation;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_periods}}: minimum number of valid observations required for an output
value.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If a row does not have enough valid observations, the output row is masked and
prints as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{as\PYGZus{}i64}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{astype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{codem}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Int64}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{as\PYGZus{}f64}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{numeric}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{astype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{codem}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Float64}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Casting rules are family\sphinxhyphen{}specific:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Series to Series changes numeric dtype.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Series to Note formats each scalar as text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Series to Timeline treats numeric values as either epoch nanoseconds or
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{YYYYMMDD}} values when all valid rows look like dates.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note to Series parses bools or numbers depending on the requested dtype.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Note to Timeline parses date/time text.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Timeline and TimeIndex can be converted to Note or numeric epoch\sphinxhyphen{}nanosecond
Series.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parsing failures become invalid rows where supported by the implementation.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

1  5
2  7
3  11
4  19

2  true

0  NA
1  1.5
2  2.333333333
3  4.666666667

dtype: Series

0  nan
1  1
2  1
3  1
4  1

1  20
2  NA
3  40

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{values + 3}} performs elementwise numeric addition. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{btw(2.0, 8.0, true)}} marks

\sphinxAtStartPar
The rolling mean uses a trailing window of three rows and requires at least two
observations. Row 0 has only one observation, so it prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NA}}. Row 1 averages
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}, giving \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.5}}. Row 4 averages \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{8}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{16}}, giving

previous value and prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nan}}; every later value doubles from the previous
